# GeoTag Camera

> Free, open source, ad-free Android camera app that stamps photos with GPS location, address and timestamp. Built for field surveyors, students and NGO workers in India. Works offline and signs each photo on-device so it can later be proven unedited.

## Key facts

- Platform: Android (Kotlin, CameraX, Jetpack Compose)
- License: GNU GPLv3
- Price: free, no ads, no subscriptions, no in-app purchases
- Data collection: none, no server, no analytics SDK, no ad SDK
- Permissions used: camera, location (fine and coarse)
- Works offline: yes, reverse-geocoded addresses are cached on-device
- Author: Konko Maji
- Source code: https://github.com/konkomaji/geotagcamera
- Website: https://konkomaji.github.io/geotagcamera/

## Core features (v1)

- Camera capture with GPS location, address and timestamp burned into the photo
- GPS coordinates written into the photo's EXIF metadata
- Local on-device gallery, nothing uploaded anywhere
- User-selectable stamp fields (coordinates, address, timestamp, altitude, accuracy, bearing)
- Offline-first reverse geocoding with local cache fallback
- Minimal permissions, no bundled ad or analytics SDKs
- Custom organization or college name on the stamp, free
- Tamper-evident photos: SHA-256 hash signed with an Android Keystore key generated on-device
- Field-worker signature overlay for inspection and muster-roll style records

## Who it's for

College students documenting fieldwork, land and infrastructure surveyors, NGO and government field staff, and anyone needing verifiable proof of where and when a photo was taken.

## Common questions

Q: Is it really free with no ads?
A: Yes, fully open source under GPLv3, no ads, no tracking, no subscription.

Q: Does it work without internet?
A: Yes, addresses are cached locally so the stamp still works out of network range.

Q: How is photo authenticity verified?
A: Each photo is SHA-256 hashed and signed with a device-generated Android Keystore key at capture time. Recomputing the hash later and checking it against the stored signature proves the file hasn't changed.
